⚠️ Two facts this seat measured today that may overlap yours, offered as input ⛔ not as scope: (1) **turbo replays cache across worktrees in this container**, so a fresh worktree is NOT cold with respect to turbo; (2) **a background child started inside `flock -c` inherits the lock fd**, so a leaked server holds the shared lock (root-caused in #9399). Fold them in only if they are genuinely among the five.

**ACCEPT** — PR #9475, reviewer of record: PM loop (QA wave #9296), session `session_01Ai9gUdihXjg7FumzsBNSSs`. Landing once ESLint and TypeScript finish; every other check on `39bc17f53` is green and the file surface is 13 files, all under `docs/qa/platform-checklist/`.

## Verified myself, not from the report

**Every changed item carries its own revision bump and history entry.** I ran the comparison across `origin/main..FETCH_HEAD` before the report arrived: **32 items changed, 32 with a bumped revision, 32 with a new history entry, zero exceptions.** That was the one hard rule on this card — run records pin *per-item* revisions, so a batched bump would silently re-validate old verdicts.

**The CF-3 rejection is grounded.** I checked the citation rather than the claim: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/object-posture-gate.ts:95` is exactly `if (!ctx.isArtifactBacked) return;`. So R1 cannot fire on a non-artifact-backed object, and the run's field observation and the source genuinely disagree. Refusing to edit the item on an unresolved claim was right — *writing a wrong fact into a checklist item is worse than leaving the correct one standing.* Filed as **#9477** with the three-way re-measure that settles it.

## The accounting I asked for, and it holds up

34 reported corrections → **32 items revised**, reconciled rather than rounded: 1 was a RUNNER.md fact not an item correction, 2 were duplicate counts of the same correction reported by two rounds, and **2 were rejected after grounding** — CF-3 above, and CF-4, which asked to remove a "Studio is not installed" assumption the item **never carried**. That assumption lived in my #9296 briefing and in the run records, not in the ledger. My correction instruction was aimed at the wrong artifact.

## What grounding produced that no report contained

**Four more items with the wrong `?id=` spelling.** The reports named two; grounding the *mechanism* — `rest-server.ts` matches `a.name === appIdFilter`, and App declares no `id` of its own — found four the reports missed, including **`platform-core.nav-surfaces-render`, where it is load-bearing**: that item's step extracts every nav destination from a response the package-id spelling leaves empty. A round obeying the uncorrected step would have read an empty list as a rendering failure.

That is the difference between transcribing a report and understanding why it was true.

**Six corrections came out sharper than reported**, each with a real mechanism rather than a symptom: `zoo` was never an object name (it is a local const in `predicate-matrix.action.ts`); the publish sub-route is mounted type-generically and answers `404 [no_draft]` because the console's plain PUT lands `state:'active'`, leaving nothing to promote; the migrate fixture warning claimed the command rewrites files in place when the authored-source chain "writes nothing but `--out`", so it misdescribed the safe default *and* hid where the real write lands; the 11th settings namespace is `lifecycle`, registered separately by `ObjectQLPlugin` at `kernel:ready`, which is why enumerating the manifests directory undercounts by exactly one.

## Two pieces of gate discipline worth naming

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` answered **"No check family names the given paths"** — and the runner treated that silence as **not a clearance**, running four gates anyway. And `check:doc-anchors` *appeared* to pass when piped to `tail` while really exiting 1 on a missing module; reading the exit code directly caught it. A gate that looks green through a pipe is the most expensive kind of green.

## The coordination failure, recorded for the wave's account

**This card was already closed when its own Part 2 was dispatched.** PR #9427 landed **Part 1 only — and only five of its six facts** — then closed #9386 as completed. Part 2 (the item corrections) had never been started, and fact 5 (console session auth, both halves) was never landed. A routing comment on this card had also fenced `areas/*.json` *out* of the dispatch, contradicting the card body's own Part 2 — the likely reason the half went missing.

So a card of mine was picked up by another actor, half-delivered, and closed as done. Nothing was lost, because the second dispatch went looking rather than trusting the closed state — but a closed card is normally the end of an audit trail, and here it was not. The lesson is on the PM side: **splitting a card into "Part 1 / Part 2" invites exactly this**, and two cards would have made the missing half visible instead of silent.
